2027-05-11.title: Seventh Tuesday of Resurrection
2027-05-11.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Do not become a stumbling block to the weak
The parable of the rich fool
2027-05-11.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta), in the days between the Ascension and Pentecost. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and the Queen of Heaven (Regina Caeli) is prayed in place of the Angelus until Pentecost. The fifth day of the novena to the Holy Spirit.
2027-05-11.verse: So it is with those who store up treasures for themselves but are not rich toward God.
theo: A man in the crowd interrupts Jesus with a family quarrel: “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the family inheritance with me.” Anyone who has lived in Kerala knows how familiar that sentence sounds. A few cents of land, a share in the ancestral house, a dispute over who looked after the parents: brothers stop speaking, cousins go to court, and sometimes the quarrel outlives everyone who began it. Jesus refuses to become the judge of the case: “Friend, who set me to be a judge or arbitrator over you?” He is not indifferent to justice; he goes to the root of the problem: “Take care! Be on your guard against all kinds of greed; for one's life does not consist in the abundance of possessions.” The word for life here is not the life of the body but life itself, the real life of a person. A house can be divided fairly and the heart still be poisoned by greed. Jesus wants to heal the heart.

Then he tells the parable of the rich man whose land produced abundantly. Notice how he speaks: “What should I do, for I have no place to store my crops?” “I will pull down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods. And I will say to my soul, Soul, you have ample goods laid up for many years; relax, eat, drink, be merry.” He talks only to himself. There is no one else in his plans: no God to thank, no neighbour to share with, no poor man at his gate. Then God speaks for the first time, and calls him by his true name: “You fool! This very night your life is being demanded of you. And the things you have prepared, whose will they be?” The answer is painfully simple: someone else's, perhaps the very brothers who will quarrel over them. Jesus ends: “So it is with those who store up treasures for themselves but are not rich toward God.” To be rich toward God is to let our goods pass through our hands into his: in thanksgiving, in almsgiving, in support for the Church and the poor. In these days before Pentecost, the Holy Spirit is the true treasure we ask for; and he is given not to those who fill their barns but to those who empty their hands.

Paul deals with a different question in Corinth, but the root is the same. Some Christians knew that idols are nothing, and so they ate meat sacrificed to idols without a second thought. Paul agrees that “food will not bring us close to God”. But he adds: “take care that this liberty of yours does not somehow become a stumbling block to the weak.” A believer whose conscience is still fragile might see a strong Christian eating in an idol's temple and be led back into idolatry. “So by your knowledge those weak believers for whom Christ died are destroyed.” The phrase cuts deep: the weak brother is one for whom Christ died. Knowledge that ignores him is not wisdom but pride; earlier in the same chapter Paul says, “Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up” (1 Corinthians 8:1). His conclusion is generous: “Therefore, if food is a cause of their falling, I will never eat meat, so that I may not cause one of them to fall.” Our rights, like our riches, are given us for others. A Christian who drinks heavily in front of a young person, who mocks the simple faith of an old woman, or who boasts of his knowledge while his neighbour stumbles, has forgotten that his brother is someone for whom Christ died.
conn: “The lover of money will not be satisfied with money; nor the lover of wealth, with gain. This also is vanity” (Ecclesiastes 5:10).
“Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked shall I return there” (Job 1:21).
“Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust consume … but store up for yourselves treasures in heaven” (Matthew 6:19–20).
“You shall not revile the deaf or put a stumbling block before the blind” (Leviticus 19:14).
Woe to the one who causes stumbling.
Jesus warns against causing one of the little ones to stumble (Matthew 18:6).
“Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up” (1 Corinthians 8:1); “Let all that you do be done in love” (1 Corinthians 16:14).
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we bring our offerings to the altar: a sign that what we have is not only for our barns but for God and for the poor. The Lord who gave his life for the weak gives himself to us, and makes us rich toward God.
At Communion we receive the Body of Christ together with the weakest members of the parish. Let us look at them as brothers and sisters for whom Christ died.
outline: A family quarrel over an inheritance, and Jesus who goes to the root.
Point 1 · Life does not consist in possessions
Greed, the poison that a fair division cannot cure.
Point 2 · You fool! This very night
The man who talked only to himself, and being rich toward God.
Point 3 · Do not become a stumbling block
Knowledge puffs up, love builds up; the weak brother for whom Christ died.
Two brothers in Kottayam who sold the disputed plot and built a house for a poor family instead.
live: If there is a quarrel over land or inheritance in your family, take one step toward peace this week: a call, a visit, a compromise.
Give away something you have stored and do not use: clothes, money, food, time.
Set aside a fixed share of your income for God and the poor, and give it with joy.
Avoid one habit, a drink, a joke, a careless word, that could make a younger or weaker person stumble.
fathers: Whom do I wrong, you say, by keeping what is mine? The bread you hold back belongs to the hungry; the coat you store in your chest belongs to the naked; the shoes rotting in your house belong to the barefoot; the money you hide away belongs to the needy. You wrong as many as you could have helped.

Not to share our own goods with the poor is to rob them and to take away their life. The goods we possess are not ours but theirs. Do not say, I use what is mine; you use what belongs to others, for all good things come from God and are given us to be shared.
magis: The tenth commandment forbids greed and the desire to amass earthly goods without limit; it forbids avarice arising from a passion for riches and their attendant power.
St John Chrysostom vigorously recalls this: “Not to enable the poor to share in our goods is to steal from them and deprive them of life. The goods we possess are not ours, but theirs.”
Scandal is an attitude or behaviour which leads another to do evil. It is grave when given by those who by nature or office are obliged to teach and educate others; Jesus utters a curse against it.
A human being must always obey the certain judgement of his conscience; conscience must be informed and moral judgement enlightened.
saints: 7–13 May: the days after the Ascension of our Lord (Thursday 6 May), when the apostles waited in prayer for the Holy Spirit “together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus” (Acts 1:14). Many families and parishes pray a novena to the Holy Spirit from Friday 7 to Saturday 15 May, the eve of Pentecost. Fri 7: First Friday. Sun 9: Seventh Sunday of Resurrection, the Sunday after the Ascension; the Latin Church in India celebrates the Ascension on this Sunday. Mon 10: in the Latin calendar, St John of Avila. Wed 12: in the Latin calendar, Sts Nereus and Achilleus and St Pancras. Thu 13: in the Latin calendar, Our Lady of Fatima. The Marian month of May continues (verify locally).
2027-05-11.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you became poor for our sake, so that by your poverty we might become rich. Guard us against every kind of greed. Heal the quarrels in our families over land and money, and teach us that our life does not consist in our possessions. Make us rich toward God by sharing what we have with the poor. Give us a love that builds up, so that we never cause a weaker brother or sister to stumble, remembering that you died for them. Send us your Holy Spirit, the true treasure, and fill our empty hands. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Jesus refuses to divide an inheritance but warns: be on your guard against all kinds of greed.
The rich fool talks only to himself; God says, This very night your life is demanded of you.
Paul: knowledge puffs up, love builds up; do not cause the weak, for whom Christ died, to stumble.
2027-05-11.action: Give away one thing you have stored and do not use, and take one step toward peace in any family quarrel over property.
2027-05-11.question: Am I storing up treasure for myself, or am I rich toward God?
kidsaint: Father Augustine Thevarparampil, whom everyone called Kunjachan (‘little father’) because he was short, was a priest of Ramapuram in Kerala. He spent his whole life visiting poor Dalit families, walking from house to house, teaching them to pray, caring for the sick and treating everyone as a child of God at a time when many looked down on them. He owned almost nothing, but he was rich toward God. He died in 1973 and was beatified in 2006. Lesson: the best treasure is the love we give away.
2027-05-11.special: Seventh Tuesday of Resurrection. Fifth day of the novena to the Holy Spirit.
term: In the Bible the skandalon is a stumbling block, something placed on the path that makes another fall. In Christian moral teaching scandal is an attitude or behaviour that leads another person to sin. Paul refuses to use even his rightful liberty if it would make a weaker believer fall (1 Corinthians 8:13); Jesus speaks severe words against those who cause the little ones to stumble.

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a rich farmer who had so much grain that he built bigger and bigger barns. He thought only about himself: ‘I will eat, drink and be happy!’ He never thought of God or of hungry people. But that night his life came to an end, and all his grain was left behind. Jesus says we should be ‘rich toward God’: sharing what we have and loving others.
family.intention: We pray for families who quarrel over money or land, that they may make peace.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family share this week with someone who has less than we do?”

illus: Two brothers in Kottayam did not speak for eleven years because of a strip of land between their houses, hardly five cents. Each was sure the plot was his. When their mother was dying, she asked them to come together to her bed and said only one thing: ‘I did not raise you to fight over mud.’ After the funeral the elder brother came to the younger with the documents and said, ‘Let neither of us have it.’ Together they gave the land to the parish, and with the help of neighbours a small house was built there for a widow and her children. The brothers say that the day the keys were handed over was the first day in eleven years they had laughed together.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you became poor to make us rich. As we gather in your name, loosen the grip of money on our hearts and open them to your Spirit. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Be on your guard against all kinds of greed (Luke 12:15). Where does greed hide in my life?
I will pull down my barns and build larger ones (Luke 12:18). What am I storing up that I could share?
This very night your life is being demanded of you (Luke 12:20). If my life were asked of me tonight, what would I wish I had done?
Take care that this liberty of yours does not somehow become a stumbling block to the weak (1 Corinthians 8:9). Has my behaviour ever made someone weaker stumble?
pm.resp: Lord, make us rich toward you.
interc: For the Church, that she may be poor in spirit and generous to all in need.
For families divided by quarrels over property and inheritance, that they may be reconciled.
For the rich and powerful, that they may use their goods for the common good.
For young people and all whose faith is fragile, that no one may cause them to stumble.
For the poor of our parish, that we may share with them as brothers and sisters.
pm.close: Father, every good gift comes from you. Teach us to hold our goods with open hands, to share them with the poor and to protect the weak, so that we may be rich toward you, through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, a man in the crowd asks Jesus, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the family inheritance with me.” How often we hear such quarrels in our own families: over land, over the house, over money.

Jesus does not take sides. He goes to the root: “Take care! Be on your guard against all kinds of greed; for one's life does not consist in the abundance of possessions.” A property can be divided fairly, and still the heart can be full of greed. Jesus wants to heal the heart.

Then he tells the story of a rich man. His land gave a great harvest, and he said: I will build bigger barns, and then I will rest, eat, drink and be merry. He spoke only to himself. No God, no neighbour, no poor man in his plans. And God said: “You fool! This very night your life is being demanded of you.” All his grain was left behind.

Paul tells the Corinthians: be careful that your liberty does not become a stumbling block to the weak. The weak brother is someone “for whom Christ died”. “Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.” Our rights and our riches are given to us for others.

In these days before Pentecost we ask for the greatest treasure, the Holy Spirit. He fills not full barns but open hands. Let us empty one barn this week, make peace in our families, and be rich toward God. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told about a man who kept all his grain for himself in big barns and never shared. God called him foolish!
Jesus wants us to be ‘rich toward God’. How? By sharing! This week, share one of your toys, snacks or pencils with someone, and you will be rich toward God.

concl: Our life is not in our barns, and our rights are given us for others.
In these days of waiting, let us empty our hands so that the Spirit may fill them.
2027-05-11.resolve: This week, make peace over property, give away what you hoard, and protect the faith of the weak.
